method: Three rounds. Each round a fresh agent that had never seen the designs matched shuffled, unlabeled black silhouettes in 6 views (side, front, 3/4 front, 3/4 rear, top, traffic ahead at 14 m) to the 12 class names, with a confidence of 1-3. Designs were revised between rounds; round 3 is the final design.
summary: Named correctly: 72 of 72 in every round (12 cars x 6 views).
Named and "sure": 33 -> 36 -> 39 of 72 as the designs were revised.
Final design, sure per view: side 12/12, 3/4 front 8/12, 3/4 rear 8/12, front 5/12, traffic ahead 5/12, top 1/12.
From the top every car is a rounded rectangle; identity from above comes from the roof graphic (glass, light bar, bed, livery), not the outline.
Audit round (revised designs, 9 views incl. 3 high angles): named correctly 106/109; every miss was at the high rear view, where the three sedans blur.

audit.method: One fresh agent, never shown the designs, matched shuffled outlines rendered by Godot (tests/fleet_silhouette_sweep.gd --save-views) to the 12 class names, 9 cameras: B1's 6 plus 3 high angles B1 never tested, picked where the 360 sweep found the closest outlines. Each outline scaled to fit its tile, so size is no cue. The high rear view had a 13th outline (the muscle sedan's street build) and the tester was told one class appeared twice. Revised designs (P2, P5, N1, P6 changed).

chase_ahead.view: traffic ahead from the chase cam

audit.note: "Sure" counts depend on the tester and the views, so they are not comparable with B1's rounds.
